audit.whatIsWrong: The layers disagreed on the last two rows: phases[5].side = Zed and phases[6].side = Skill, while win[5] and win[6] both read Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: At 45.48% over 919 games this is a losing matchup, so handing Aurelion Sol both item stages overstates it. Zed owns 1 through 6, the first-item stage is genuinely close once Rod of Ages health lands, and only the two-item stage is clearly Aurelion Sol's.
audit.corrected: Zed / Zed / Zed / Zed / Zed / Skill / Aurelion Sol, proposed as matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named 'Starsurge', 'Voice of Light' and a 'Rocketbelt' first item, and wants.foe[0] referenced a 'Q stun'.
audit.why: None exist: the current Aurelion Sol runs Breath of Light, Astral Flight, the black hole and Falling Star / The Skies Descend, his Q has no stun, and the itemization section of this very page builds Rod of Ages or Seraph's, not Rocketbelt.
audit.corrected: Spikes and wants rebuilt on the real kit and the real build path, with Razor Shuriken's 900 range against the beam's 750, Living Shadow's 20s and Death Mark's 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death Mark's untargetability, the three-second mark timer, and the fact that Zed has no channel interrupt were all absent.
audit.why: Death Mark makes Zed untargetable during the dash, so holding Falling Star to stop the commit wastes a 120-second ultimate — Zhonya's during the three seconds before the mark repeats his damage is the actual answer. Conversely, Zed's only CC is Shadow Slash's slow, so nothing in his kit cancels Breath of Light or Astral Flight: the beam gets to finish if you can afford to stand there.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[4], spikes[1], mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.
sources: enemyKit (R: untargetable, dash; E: slow only)

audit.whatIsWrong: The brief's missingInteractions claims Astral Flight 'shuts off Zed's Living Shadow and Death Mark'.
audit.why: That derives from a terrain flag on Astral Flight, but Riot's own description says Aurelion Sol flies OVER terrain — it does not say he creates any. Per the calibration rule I trusted the description and asserted nothing about wall-blocking his dashes.
audit.corrected: Left out of every edit; recorded here and in notes so it can be verified before anyone writes it.

edits.after: Razor Shuriken chunks you from 900 units against your 750, and Living Shadow on a 20-second cooldown lets him leave before your beam has burned two seconds.

edits.before: Death Mark one-shot potential spikes hard here — if he lands it on you while you're pushed up, you're dead before your ult can even land.
edits.after: Death Mark's dash is untargetable, so nothing you hold answers the commit; the mark repeats his damage after three seconds — that is Zhonya's window.

edits.before: A completed Rocketbelt/first item finally gives you the burst and range to punish his cooldowns and threaten his Death Mark window back.
edits.after: Rod of Ages or Seraph's finally gives the health to survive the mark, and E executes clear waves without stepping into shuriken range.

edits.before: Your uncapped AP scaling, global ult presence, and Voice of Light poke outclass a Zed who falls off without consistent kills to snowball.
edits.after: Your uncapped Stardust, The Skies Descend, and a beam that never stops growing outclass a Zed who falls off without kills to snowball.

edits.before: Zed's Q-W harass chips you down from outside your effective trading range, and he can weave in and out with Shadow before your slow-windup Starsurge ever lands. Levels 1-5 you're mostly surviving — freezing, taking short trades only when his shadow is on cooldown, and avoiding overextending since a landed Death Mark at 6 can delete you outright.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken chips you from 900 units, outside your 750-unit beam, and Living Shadow lets him weave in and out on a 20-second cooldown at rank 1. Levels 1-5 you are surviving — freeze, trade only when his shadow is down, and never be pushed up at 6, because a landed Death Mark deletes you outright. Zed has no hard CC, so at least the beam itself never gets cancelled.

edits.before: Level 6 is Zed's biggest spike: Death Mark plus a shadow swap gives him burst that can one-shot you if he catches you pushed up or out of position, and his shadow escape means your ult rarely punishes him back. Play centrally near allies, keep vision on his roam paths, and never let him get a free flank angle on you.
edits.after: Level 6 is Zed's biggest spike: Death Mark is untargetable on the way in, so Falling Star cannot stop it and holding your ult for the dash wastes 120 seconds. The mark repeats his damage three seconds later — that is exactly what Zhonya's buys you. Play centrally, ward his roam paths, and never give him a free flank angle.

edits.before: Once you hit your first item your range and stun uptime finally let you zone him and punish his cooldowns directly, and by full build your scaling AP damage and global ultimate outclass a Zed whose damage plateaus without kill snowball. Survive lane, group with your team, and let your late-game power carry.
edits.after: Once you hit your first item, your beam range and Falling Star uptime finally let you zone him and punish Living Shadow's downtime directly, and by full build your Stardust scaling and The Skies Descend outclass a Zed whose damage plateaus without kill snowball. Survive lane, group with your team, and let your late-game power carry.

edits.before: Poke you down with Q-W from max range where you can't threaten a Q stun
edits.after: Poke you down with Razor Shuriken from 900 units, outside your beam

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Astral Flight like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Death Mark: 120s at rank 1, untargetable on the dash — the answer is Zhonya's during the three-second mark, not your R. - Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1: with it down he can neither engage nor leave. - Nothing in his kit cancels your channel.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by scaling honestly — Stardust is permanent, and a Zed without kills is a melee champion trying to reach a 750-unit beam.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Zed on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the reset: Astral Flight's cooldown drops when an enemy champion dies, so a Zed who commits and loses hands you back your escape and the next wave.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Zed wins by shuriken-chipping you from 900 units, then Death Marking the health bar he already lowered.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Freezing keeps you in tower range for the three seconds the mark ticks — the difference between dying and Zhonya's.

edits.before: Zed burns Death Mark on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Zed burns Death Mark elsewhere — that is a two-minute invitation.

edits.before: That’s Zed’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: He has no interrupt, but he does not need one from inside 290 units.
